line: Clip in the stick, stick in the coat (Boom)
vault_lines: Clip in the stick, stick in the coat (Boom)
meaning:
“Clip in the stick” is slang for “ammo in the firearm”, meaning that the gun is loaded with ammunition.



Stick in the coat means that the “stick” aka a rifle is inside the coat. This continues the Russian nesting doll/inception theme of this particular line.

vault_lines: Please don't think it's a joke
meaning:
Fronto is a raw tobacco leaf used to roll marijuana. It is Brooklyn drill’s favorite blunt wrap.

It had been referenced frequently in the drill rap sense. Probably most notably was Rowdy Rebel on “Computers”, his 2014 collab with Bobby Shmurda where he said:

Smoking Fronto, bitch no Phillies

American comedian, Kevin Hart, is 1.63 m (5'4") and often makes jokes about himself being short and small.

line: Got the ladies hittin’ my phone (Brr) Got the mandem hittin’ the woah (Greaze) Me plus ten on the list, they know how I’m comin’, I’m bringin’ the bros
vault_lines: Got the ladies hittin' my phone (Brr)
meaning:
Skepta is describing the activities of his close crew, the girls yearning to be around him and the guys he brings to all his events. Mandem is UK slang for a group of men or crew who are, hitting the woah, a dance move that became widely popular in 2018.



This line is also a reference to Skepta’s 2016 track “Ladies Hit Squad” which is an ode to romancing fine ladies.

line: Dream on, fly away (Yeah), dream on (Uh)

meaning:
Dream On is the name of Cudi’s now-dissolved  record label.  The label was originally founded in 2009 with long-time friends and producers Plain Pat and Emile Haynie, but was short-lived as it dissolved in February 2011.

Despite the label fading away, Cudi has never stopped dreaming on.

line: Left wrist Audemars Piguet, right wrist whippin’ the whip on the stove He don’t care ’bout fame, he just tryna get rich on the low
vault_lines: Left wrist Audemars Piguet, right wrist whippin' the whip on the stove
meaning:
“Whippin' the whip on the stove” is related to a common phrase which refers to the process of cooking crack. The process roughly consists of adding ice to a mixture of boiled cocaine and baking soda, then vigorously whipping to quickly cool it until it coagulates into crack.  This method of cutting cocaine has been used for decades as a way to get rich quickly.



This line mirrors a lyric from Pusha T’s track “Drug Dealers Anonymous”, in which Jay Z raps:

Life made me ambidextrous
Countin’ with my right, whippin’ white with my left wrist

line: Back on tour with the gang and it’s sold out Twenty-two dates, I ain’t missin’ a show
vault_lines: Back on tour with the gang and it's sold out
meaning: Prior to the 2020 global pandemic, Skepta was busy touring.  Skepta put on shows in exactly 22 different locations across the world throughout 2019, as reported by Resident Advisor.  As he traveled from the UK to Australia, he didn’t miss a show, and based on his recent tour reviews, he certainly “show[ed] out” as well. Pop Smoke was also the supporting act for the four UK dates of Skepta’s 2019 ‘Ignorance Is Bliss’ tour. These were Pop Smoke’s only and last performances outside of the US.

line: All my niggas is ready to go Pop Smoke, big smoke
vault_lines: All my niggas is ready to go
meaning:
This is a possible reference to the only known footage of Pop Smoke and Skepta together.

In the clip Skepta says “Big Pop” and Pop Smoke responds “Yeah! Big Smoke… Pop Smoke!” which acknowledges the similarity between his artist name and Skepta’s moniker ‘Big Smoke’.

Skepta may be referring to what Pop Smoke said, responding by flipping the order of the names, possibly as a sign of respect or tribute.
